answer: Escrowed Beacon Decay. Each identity posts a small refundable deposit plus a per-period carrying charge; the charge is credited to a public beacon that decays unless the identity's activity reconfirms it. Cloning forces an attacker to fund every copy's carrying charge indefinitely, so cost scales linearly with identity count. A knoll of idle clones collapses in a few periods. Sustained presence near a summit requires continuous outlay, but honest single identities recoup their deposit.
